title: Plan-aware admission prefetch and hedged fallbacks for tiered routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We observe increased latency and failed requests when free-tier traffic hits burst windows and the system immediately tries to route to paid/enterprise pools or fall back to cheaper model variants. This ticket explores a combined approach: (1) a small, plan-aware prefetch queue that warms KV caches and model variants optimistically for expected cross-tier handoffs, and (2) a hedged fallback mechanism that runs a lightweight fast-path variant while concurrently attempting a higher-quality variant for a short window. Goal: reduce user-visible latency and error rates during quota-driven demotions without over-consuming paid capacity or violating plan quotas. Scope: admission logic changes, a prefetching worker, hedged request orchestration, metrics/tracing, and a conservative rollout with feature flag and canary by org tier.
acceptance_criteria: Prefetch queue warms KV cache or model snapshot for ~85% of identified cross-tier handoffs within configured window
Hedged fallback executes fast-path variant within 50ms P50 while attempting high-quality variant; final response picks highest-quality result within 300ms or fast-path result if none
Routing respects plan quotas: prefetch budget is bounded per-customer and charged to a separate prefetch budget counter
No increase in paid-tier token consumption beyond configured safety multiplier (default 1.15) during canary
End-to-end tests and synthetic traffic demonstrate <10% user-visible failure rate reduction during simulated quota-exhaustion events
Dashboard and tracing show per-org metrics for prefetch usage, hedged request wins, and additional cost attribution
notes: Design trade-offs: aggressive prefetch reduces latency but risks over-allocating paid tokens. We'll cap per-org prefetch budget and expose a tuning knob in Console.
We prefer optimistic prefetch tied to observed transfer patterns (e.g., recent spike in requests from free->paid within 2 minutes) rather than universal prefetch to limit waste.
Hedged fallback leverages existing fast-path model variants (quantized, shorter context) to minimize extra cost and latency; winning criteria include log-prob threshold and token budget.

Fallback composition: if fast-path returns and high-quality still in-flight, return fast-path for latency-sensitive endpoints (chat streaming) and replace with HQ for batch endpoints if arrives within budget.
This ticket intentionally does not change billing model; cost attribution will be surfaced but billing changes are separate follow-up.
Coordination: requires minor console UI for prefetch knobs and an observability dashboard (see design_links).
engineering_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike complete. Measured 180ms median cold-start KV latency for cross-variant requests on g5. Baseline traced.
2026-02-20: Implemented prefetch worker prototype and added prefetch budget counter to tenant-metadata store. Initial unit tests passing.
2026-02-28: Hedged request orchestrator merged behind feature flag. Added synthetic harness to fire quota-exhaustion scenarios.
2026-03-05: Canary started for 100 orgs on staging; observed prefetch hit-rate 72% and hedged-win-rate 38%. Need to tune selection heuristics.
2026-03-10: Adjusted prefetch heuristics to use short-term spike detector (EWMA) and increased hedging timeout to 220ms for batch endpoints. Metrics dashboard panels added.
test_plan: Unit tests for prefetch budget accounting and eviction logic
Integration test simulating quota-exhaustion and verifying hedged outcome selection
Load test with mixed free/paid traffic and region-affinity to ensure no cross-region over-prefetching
Chaos test: kill HQ variant container during hedged window and confirm graceful degrade to fast-path
Cost sim: run 24h synthetic to estimate extra paid-token consumption at different prefetch budgets
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable feature flag for 5% of orgs (low-risk, high-observability) with strict paid-token safety multiplier
Phase 2: expand to 25% after 72h if paid-token increase < 5% and failure rates drop as expected
Phase 3: tenant-level control exposed in Console; allow opt-out and budget tuning
Rollback: feature flag kill switches prefetch and hedging immediately; circuit-breaker trips if paid-tier consumption exceeds threshold
followups: PM to evaluate billing model changes for charging prefetch token consumption (PM-3702)
Design: sketch UX for per-tenant prefetch budget controls and explainers (DES-403)
Observability: add long-term retention for hedged metrics and cost attribution in infra billing pipeline
